| Field | Value |
|---|---|

| Section | Ops |

| Tags | `ops`, `agents`, `uv`, `langgraph`, `crewai`, `autogen`, `o-05` |

## Problem

Category o-05 is the agent-framework shelf: langgraph, crewai and
autogen as catalogue rows, `uv` as the environment tool that keeps
their (versioned, mutually-versioned) pins clean. You want one,
repeatable scaffold: pin an interpreter, create per-project
environments, install a framework surface, and prove the imports
work before wiring a scanner or a defence onto it.

## Solution

Work the stack row by row; `uv` manages every environment:

```bash
# 0. Confirm the rows (o-05 langgraph/crewai/autogen + uv)
kailash info langgraph
kailash info crewai

# 1. interpreter + env (python 3.13 rides the pinned stack)
uv self list        # (uv is the manifest row; 0.11.x at the pin)
uv init agents-lab && cd agents-lab
uv python install 3.13
uv venv --python 3.13

# 2. langgraph surface (framework row, safety safe o-05)
uv add "langgraph>=1.1.10"

# 3. crewai surface — it has its OWN CLI + project flow:
uv tool install crewai            # the tool runner, uv-managed
crewai create crew my-crew        # JSON-first scaffold (see Discussion)
crewai install && crewai run      # the pinned flow

# 4. autogen surface — extension packages + a locked sync
uv add "autogen-agentchat" "autogen-ext[openai]"
uv add "crewai==1.14.4" "langchain==1.2.15" "langgraph==1.1.10"
uv sync --all-extras              # autogen's declared install surface

# 5. import smoke — the CI check, worked by hand:
uv run python - <<'EOF'
import langchain, langgraph, crewai
import autogen_agentchat, autogen_ext
print("ok: all o-05 imports landed")
EOF
```

Expected output shape (abridged, shapes not transcripts):

```
# step 5 is the pass/fail gate
ok: all o-05 imports landed   # -> exit 0
# crewai scaffold shape
my-crew/
  config/*.yaml  src/my_crew/  pyproject.toml(?)
```

## Discussion

- **Why uv and not pip-by-hand:** the o-05 rows version against each
  other (langchain 1.2.15, langgraph 1.1.10, crewai 1.14.4 and
  autogen's sub-packaging at the pin), and a locked, per-project
  environment is the cheapest way to keep those pins reproducible;
  uv 0.11.x also carries the `uv tool` flow crewai prefers. One
  python (3.13) across the lab keeps `uv sync` honest.
- **Import smoke rides CI in this book:** the guide's CI runs the
  same check as step 5 (import of each landed framework package);
  doing it by hand closes the gap between "the package downloaded"
  and "the stack imports". Any smoke failure is a pin problem —
  read the lock, not the network.
- **The autogen maintenance-mode note, honestly:** upstream marks
  some autogen subpackages in maintenance mode (the main project's
  own communication); the row still ships (agentchat + ext[openai]
  install cleanly via
  `uv sync --all-extras`). The honest posture:
  pin by version, keep surfaces small, and treat upstream's
  maintenance-mode announcements as a real signal — do not build a
  new multi-year surface on a maintenance-mode subpackage.
- **crewai is JSON-first by design:** the `crewai create crew`
  scaffold keeps crew definitions as config (YAML/JSON), with
  `crewai install && crewai run` as the flow. The CLI is the
  manifest's declared surface — not a library-only import.
- **The exp MCP rows stay gated — this recipe touches them not at
  all:** several o-07-adjacent MCP tools (`kailash-mcp`,
  `kailash-container`) are `safety.level: exp`. They install only
  through the double-key lab gate and its wrapped paths (see
  [Gate lab-mode and exp-classified tools](../admin/lab-mode-gating.html)),
  and every one is gate-wrapped via
  `kailash.safety.extraTools`). An o-05 lab that "works"
  with an exp row un-wrapped is broken on any hardened host — keep
  the gate in the loop and name the row's gate status in your
  lab notes.
- **langgraph's install surface:** the row is the pip/uv package
  (`uv add langgraph`), no CLI — its recipes are graph-as-code.
